articles.title: Evening with Manchester United Treble Winners Scheduled for October 23 at Middleton Arena
articles.excerpt: Football fans can meet Manchester United legends Andy Cole, Denis Irwin, and David May at Middleton Arena for a special event on October 23, hosted by Alan Keegan.
articles.content_html:
Football fans will have the opportunity to relive the glory days of Manchester United's treble-winning season at a special event at Middleton Arena on October 23. The event, titled 'An Evening With The Treble Winners', will feature three key figures from the club's historic 1998-1999 squad: Andy Cole, Denis Irwin, and David May.

The evening will be hosted by Alan Keegan, known as the voice of Old Trafford, who will guide the audience through interviews and anecdotes from the players. Attendees can expect to hear behind-the-scenes stories and insights from the players who played pivotal roles in securing the Premier League, FA Cup, and Champions League titles under Sir Alex Ferguson.

Middleton Arena described the event as a unique chance to get up close with football icons, stating, "Three icons. One night. A lifetime of Old Trafford glory in the spotlight." This event promises to be a memorable experience for both lifelong Manchester United supporters and general football enthusiasts alike.

Tickets for the event are expected to be in high demand, and fans are encouraged to secure their seats early to avoid disappointment. Further details regarding ticket availability can be found on the Middleton Arena website.

articles.title: Two Women Arrested After Three-Year-Old Boy Falls from Window in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Two women, aged 19 and 20, have been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury to a child after a three-year-old boy fell from a window in Rochdale and remains in critical condition.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

Two women, aged 19 and 20, have been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury to a child after a three-year-old boy fell from a window in Rochdale and remains in critical condition.

A three-year-old boy is in critical condition after falling from a first-floor window in Spotland Tops, Rochdale. Two women, aged 19 and 20, have been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury to a child.

Two women have been arrested following a serious incident involving a three-year-old boy who fell from a window in Rochdale. The incident occurred on Saturday, August 22, at a property located in Spotland Tops, in the Cutgate area of the town. Emergency services were called to the scene shortly after 4.15pm, responding to reports of concern for the welfare of a child.

Upon arrival, police and paramedics found the boy had sustained critical injuries from the fall. An air ambulance was also deployed to assist in transporting the child to hospital, where he remains in a critical condition. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) confirmed that the boy fell from a first-floor window of the property.

On Sunday, August 23, GMP announced the arrest of two women, aged 19 and 20, at a property in Blackburn. They were taken into custody on suspicion of causing serious injury to a child. The police have stated that inquiries into the full circumstances surrounding the incident are ongoing.

This incident has raised significant concern within the local community, and further updates from GMP are expected as the investigation progresses. Anyone with information related to the incident is encouraged to come forward to assist the police.

articles.title: Northern Care Alliance Declares Critical Incident Ahead of Strikes
articles.excerpt: The Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust has declared a critical incident as over 350 workers prepare to strike at hospitals including Rochdale Infirmary, impacting surgeries and treatments.
articles.content_html:
The Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust (NCA) has declared a critical incident in response to upcoming strikes by healthcare workers. The strikes, involving more than 350 staff members, are scheduled to take place at Salford Royal Hospital, Royal Oldham Hospital, Rochdale Infirmary, and Fairfield Hospital in Bury on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday of this week.

The decision to declare a critical incident aims to secure additional support to maintain urgent surgical services, although some procedures will be postponed. The strikes are part of an ongoing dispute over pay related to staffing shortages, with Unison indicating a willingness to negotiate with the trust.

The NCA has apologised for the disruption this may cause to patients and has assured that those affected by changes to their surgery, treatment, or appointments will be contacted directly. Patients are advised not to call the hospitals to check on their appointments, as the trust will reach out to them.

This critical incident declaration highlights the ongoing challenges faced by the NHS in Greater Manchester, particularly in light of staffing issues and the impact of industrial action on healthcare services. The situation will be monitored closely as the strikes proceed.
